question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for 'protection against arrest and detention in certain cases’?
solution:
The correct answer is __Article 22.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Article 22 - Protection against arrest and detention 

 
 
• No person, who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice. 
 
• Every person, who is arrested and detained in custody is to be produced before the nearest Magistrate within a period of 24 hours of arrest and such person cannot be detained in custody beyond that period without the authority of a Magistrate.
 
• Article 22 is not available to an enemy alien and a person arrested or detained under a law providing for preventive detention (detention of a person without trial). 
 
• The detention of a person cannot exceed three months under the Preventive Detention Law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Article 10 **of the Constitution of India states that Any person who is considered a citizen of India under any of the provisions of this Part shall continue to be citizens and will also be subject to any law made by the Parliament
 
• **Article 47** of the Constitution of India directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.
 
• ** Article 35** of the Constitution of India provides for the power of the Parliament to make laws with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List.
